name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: SMW5 cable fault off Pakistan since 18 Nov
summary: A fault on the SMW5 cable off Pakistan since 18 Nov slows internet; GPS jamming hit Dutch flights on 16 Nov
state: A fault on the SMW5 submarine cable about 11km off Pakistan's coast caused slow speeds and intermittent connectivity from 18 Nov, with HTTP traffic down by as much as 36% per Cloudflare Radar; the cause is not yet known (The National; Radio Pakistan, citing PTA, 19 Nov). Separately, suspected GPS jamming disrupted navigation for dozens of aircraft over the Netherlands and Belgium on 16 Nov (VRT). A cable damage incident and GNSS interference keep Watch.
for_you: Internet users and businesses in Pakistan may see slower connections until repairs are complete. Airlines and pilots follow national aviation authority notices on GNSS interference; passengers are not reported to be at risk.
rubric_hit: Cable damage incident (SMW5) and GNSS interference = Watch; no confirmed sabotage

sources.title: The National — Pakistan internet problems after subsea cable fault
Radio Pakistan — Submarine cable fault may affect internet services: PTA
VRT NWS — GPS signals from dozens of aircraft over Belgium and the Netherlands disrupted

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
